summary: The current implementation is biologically morphology-neutral by design and in focused source-level tests: unusual short, long, wide, thin, curved, tortuous, low-ratio, and single-slice morphology remains eligible, WT morphology is not used as a comparative acceptance target, and manual correction reasons cannot exclude morphology alone. Report-generation code distinguishes estimated sampled-ROI quantities from whole-organ quantities and withholds biological inference for inadequate specimen replication. Acceptance remains blocked because the claim's retained report and validation receipt predate material changes to primary width, merge splitting, and estimated nucleus counts. The repository explicitly labels those measurements as superseded and states that no current full-stack replay supports them. Consequently, current biological report behavior and phenotype preservation after the new merge-splitting logic are not demonstrated by commit-bound production evidence.

findings.title: Current production semantics lack a commit-bound full-stack biological replay and report package
findings.impact: The new objective merge-splitting behavior changes estimated nucleus counts differently in the two pilot specimens, while primary width and report surfaces also changed. Without a current full-stack replay and reconciled report package, the review cannot establish that thresholds preserve the studied phenotype or that the production report reflects commit 681a5f3. This blocks the high-risk production-candidate claim.
evidence: V5_7_1_VALIDATION_REPORT.md:95-98 reports plane-35 count increases of 12.7% in KJ-01 and 7.1% in WT-01 after the merge-splitting change.
V5_7_1_VALIDATION_REPORT.md:157-167 limits current signal-width evidence to three sampled planes and says it is not a substitute for a fresh audited run.
V5_7_1_VALIDATION_REPORT.md:212-220 states the prior replay no longer describes the current pipeline and no biological conclusion may rest on its numbers.
audits/validation/v571_6f9e73b_validation.md is bound to older production commit `6f9e73b170db121460ab82f28542d1ed1e8f96bb`.

audits/evidence/v571_rc6_candidate/report/01_biological_results/data/biological_statistical_tests.csv still reports the superseded mask-width and projection-based measurement surface rather than the current signal-FWHM and representative-section contract.
findings.recommendation: Generate a commit-bound full-stack replay for both representative specimens using commit 681a5f3, rebuild biological and QC reports from those outputs, validate report-to-source consistency, and provide stratified before/after counts for short, 15-20 um, above-20-um, single-slice, morphology-warning, split, and technical-failure populations by specimen. A new superseding audit must review that evidence.

findings.title: Objective merge rules still require external biological validation
findings.impact: Branch topology and profile bimodality are technically defensible separation evidence, but they have not been shown against independent manual instance masks across WT and mutant morphology. True branched or overlapping biological configurations could therefore be split or excluded differentially.

findings.recommendation: Validate merge classification and splitting against blinded manual instance masks from multiple independent WT and mutant specimens, reporting false-split and missed-merge rates stratified by morphology and genotype. Until then, describe merge-derived counts as technically reconstructed estimates.

findings.impact: The available report contains only one specimen per group; nucleus-level observations cannot substitute for independent biological specimens.

limitations: No full image stack was run, as instructed.
Focused pytest execution could not start because the managed read-only environment had no writable temporary directory.
Other reviewers' outputs were not read. Historical audit reviews were excluded as decision evidence.
Manual-mask biological ground truth and external validation cohorts were not available in the reviewed evidence.
The retained full-stack evidence represents one pilot specimen per group and predates current merge and primary-width semantics.
